data.narrative:
Runpod, a Series C chip and semiconductor company that has raised $122.3M to date, is valued here using a two-method triangulation anchored to a peer set of 4 same-sector, same/adjacent-stage private companies (Tenstorrent at $2.7B Series D, d-Matrix at $2.0B Series C, Positron AI at $1.0B Series B, and DEEPX at $529M Series C) alongside 3 public semiconductor comparables (ALAB, NVDA, AMD).

The Stage-Progression method applies a 1.7x step-up multiplier typical of Series C advancement to the $122M total raised proxy, yielding $208M. The Peer-Median method anchors to the $1.5B median valuation across the 4 private peers, with a range spanning $529M to $2.7B. Public-Comp Anchoring using the 21.0x price-to-sales median observed in the semiconductor sector cannot be applied due to unavailable revenue figures for the target.

Triangulation across the two applicable methods produces a valuation range of $177M (low) to $1.7B (high), with a median of $854M. The substantial width reflects genuine uncertainty: stage-progression yields a conservative estimate rooted in capital deployment, while peer-median reflects the demonstrated valuations of comparable chip-focused entities at proximate funding stages. Key sensitivities include Runpod's relative progress toward revenue generation and capital efficiency versus the peer cohort, neither of which can be quantified from available data.
